rationale: The workflow is a release workflow triggered on `create` that builds two required release artifacts in parallel (Ubuntu deb and Rockylinux rpm). I evaluated the applicable evidence patterns: P-LIT-FAIL-FAST (cancel remaining matrix jobs after failure) is contraindicated because every matrix outcome is a required release artifact, so cancelling the sibling job on failure would reduce intended build coverage and the prerequisite that remaining results are dispensable is not met. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (bound jobs with a custom timeout) cannot be safely applied because there is no representative successful-duration history (ci_history shows no completed runs), so a safe timeout bound cannot be derived and valid slow release builds risk being timed out. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (cache dependency downloads) lacks a clear separate measurable dependency-download step or lockfile outside the Docker image build, so the cache-inputs/lockfile precondition is not satisfied. No supported optimization preserves the intended build and test coverage here.
